steps.text: Wash cells once with room temperature PBS.
Collect cells with a cell scraper in 1~m ice-cold PBS and transfer into a 1.5m microcentrifuge tube.
Pellet cells at 130xg in a refrigerated centrifuge at 4^°C for 3 min.
Lrase cell pellet with 5 volumes of ice-cold E1 buffer for 1 volume of cell pellet.
Pipet gently up and down (5 times) before centrifugation at 1,100xg at 4^°C for 2 min.
Collect the supernatant in a fresh tube (cytoplasm fraction).
Resuspend the pellet by gentle pipetting with the same volume of E1 buffer used for the previous step (Step 4).
Centrifuge immediately at 1,100xg at 4^°C for 2 min.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the pellet by gentle pipetting with the same volume of E1 buffer used for the previous step (Step 4).
Leave the tube for 10 min on ice.
Centrifuge at 1,100xg at 4^°C for 2 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet by gentle pipetting in 2 volumes of ice-cold E2 buffer for 1 volume of cell pellet.
Centrifuge at 1,100xg at 4^°C for 2 min.
Collect the supernatant in a fresh tube (nucleus fraction).
Resuspend the pellet with the same volume of E2 buffer used for the previous step (Step 13).
Centrifuge immediately at 1,100xg at 4^°C for 2 min.
Resuspend the pellet keeping the same volume of E2 used for the previous step (Step 13).
Leave the tube for 10 min on ice.
Centrifuge at 1,100xg at 4^°C for 2 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet by pipetting in ice-cold E3 buffer (same volume as used for E1 in Step 4).
Sonicate in a water bath sonicator with ice for 5 min, 30 sec ON/30 sec OFF on maximum power.
Centrifuge all the fractions at 16,000×g at 4^°C for 10 min.
Transfer each supernatant into fresh microcentrifuge tubes.
Measure protein concentration and proceed to Western blot analysis.
Resuspend the pellet in ice-cold E3 (benzonase) buffer (same volume as used for E1 in Step 4).
Flick the tube to detach the pellet.
Add benzonase at a 1:1,000 dilution.
Place the tube on a rotating platform and leave to rotate at 15 rpm for 20 min at room temperature.
Centrifuge all the fractions at 16,000×g at 4^°C for 10 min.
Transfer each supernatant into fresh microcentrifuge tubes.
Measure protein concentration and proceed to required pull-down assay.
Collect lung post-mortem biopsies and fix them for three hours at RT in 4% formaldehyde.
Dehydration: Eliminate the fixation agent by successive baths of increasing ethanol concentration.
Clearing: Immerse the tissues in a xylene bath three times for 20 minutes.
Embed in liquid paraffin at 59°C.
Cut 4-um-thick tissue sections using a rotary microtome and place on Superfrost slides.
Rinse the slides in Neo Clear twice for 10 minutes.
Place the slides in a 100% ethanol bath for 5 minutes.
Place the slides in a 96% ethanol bath for 5 minutes.
Place the slides in an 80% ethanol bath for 5 minutes.
Place the slides in a 70% ethanol bath for 5 minutes.
Place the slides in a 50% ethanol bath for 5 minutes.
Rinse in ultrapure distilled water three times for one minute.
Rinse in 1× PBS.
Place the slides in a vertical, plastic staining rack and add antigen retrieval buffer.
Fill the sterilizer with an adequate amount of distilled water.
Place the rack in the sterilizer and close it.
Allow the sterilizer to heat to 120-135°C and incubate for 10-15 minutes.
After 10-15 minutes, open the lid and allow the slides to cool to RT on the bench for approximately 20 minutes.
Rinse twice with 1× PBS.
Immerse the slides in permeabilization buffer for 2 minutes.
Rinse twice with 1× PBS.
Place the slides in the staining rack and incubate with blocking buffer for one hour at RT.
Keep the excess blocking buffer at 4°C.
During the blocking step, prepare the StainTray slide staining system.
Rinse the slides once with 1× PBS.
Prepare the primary staining mix.
Place the slides in the staining system tray.
Place the staining mix on the tissue sections to completely immerse them.
Close the staining system and incubate at RT for one hour.
Transfer the slides to a plastic rack.
Rinse three times with 1× PBS.
Prepare the secondary staining mix.
Place the slides in the staining system tray.
Place the staining mix on the tissue sections to completely immerse them.
Close the staining system and incubate for two hours at RT.
Transfer the slides to a plastic rack.
Rinse three times with 1× PBS.
Remove the moistened paper from the staining system tray.
Dry the slides.
Place a drop of ProLong Gold onto the tissue sections and add a coverslip.
Allow the slides to dry overnight, protected from the light.
Analyze the slides and acquire images using a confocal microscope within two days of staining.
Perform primary staining with isotype control antibodies.
Replace the primary staining with an incubation with sera from the host species.

Germinate tomato seeds (Solanum lycopersicum Mill. cv. Ailsa Craig) in pots (50~ml) with 100% vermiculite in a growth room under the following environmental conditions: light/dark cycle of 16/8~h, temperature of 24/18^°C, light intensity of 200 umol m^-2 s^-1, and relative humidity of 60%.
Irrigate seeds twice a week with approximately 50ml/pot of distilled water during 1 week.
Irrigate seedlings twice each week for 3 weeks with approximately 50~ml/pot of nutrient solution.
Supply N in the form of (NH4)2SO4 0.33g/L.
Adjust the pH of the nutrient solution to 6.0 with 1 mM KOH.
Divide 20 uniform tomato plants into two groups (10 plants are not treated and 10 plants are treated with the inhibitor solution).
Treat 21-day-old tomato plants with 2~ml of the inhibitor mix by soil drench (final concentration in each pot is DMFA 80 nM and DFMO 200 nM).
Treat 23-day-old tomato plants with 4ml of the inhibitor mix by soil drench (final concentration in each pot is DMFA 160 nM and DFMO 400 nM).
Treat 25-day-old and 27-day-old tomato plants with 8ml of the inhibitor mix (final concentration in each pot is DMFA 320 nM and DFMO 800 nM).
Collect the 3rd and 4th true leaves of treated or not treated tomato plants 24h after the last treatment.
Store the collected leaves at -80~^°C.
Crush a pool of 10 plants in liquid N2 in a mortar and use 0.2 for putrescine extraction.
Perform three biological replicates.
Quantify putrescine following the protocol of Sanchez-Lopez et al. (2009) by ion pair LC coupled with electrospray tandem mass spectrometry.
Express putrescine content as the average of three independent experiments (Fernández-Crespo et al., 2015).
Pick a single colony of Salmonella cells expressing pHluorin(M153R)-FliG from LB agar plate and inoculate it into a glass test tube with 5mL of medium and shaking at 150 rpm at 30°C overnight.
Add ampicillin to a final concentration of 100 μg/mL when SJW1368/pYVM008 cells are grown.
Transfer 50 μL of overnight culture to 5 mL of fresh TB and incubate at 30°C with shaking at 150 rpm until the cell density reaches an OD_600 of ca. 1.8.
Transfer 500 μL of each culture to a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube and collect the cells by centrifugation (6,000 × g, 2 min).
Discard supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1.0 mL of motility buffer.
Centrifuge at 6,000 × g for 2 min and discard supernatant. Repeat this step twice.
Make a tunnel slide by sandwiching double-sided tape between a 24 × 32 mm coverslip (bottom side) and an 18 × 18 mm coverslip (top side).
Add 50 μL of the cell suspension to the tunnel slide and leave for 5 min to attach the cells to the coverslip surface.
Wash out unbound cells by supplying 100 μL of motility buffer using a pipette and absorb excess buffer with filter paper.
Put the sample on a custom-built inverted fluorescence microscope.
Select a 150 × objective and insert a 1.6 × variable lens.

Switch between 410 and 470 nm excitation filters using a high-speed wavelength switcher and capture each image of the pHluorin(M153R)-FliG fluorescent spots by the EMCCD camera with a 5 sec exposure time.
Resuspend SJW1368 cells carrying pYVM008 in 500 μL of motility buffer containing 20 μM gramicidin and 20 mM potassium benzoate.
Add 50 μL of the cell suspension to the tunnel slide and leave for 5 min.
Wash out unbound cells by supplying 100 μL of motility buffer containing 20 μM gramicidin and 20 mM potassium benzoate and absorb excess buffer with filter paper.

Put the sample on the fluorescence microscope and acquire ratiometric fluorescence images of the cells at external pH 6.0, 6.5, 7.0, or 7.5 in the presence of 20 μM gramicidin and 20 mM potassium benzoate.
Suspend purified pHluorin(M153R)-FliG proteins in motility buffer with distinct pH values (5.5, 6.0, 6.5, 7.0, 7.5, 8.0, or 8.5).
Add 50 μL of the solution containing pHluorin(M153R)-FliG proteins to the tunnel slide and absorb excess solution with filter paper.
Acquire fluorescence images of the pHluorin(M153R)-FliG protein solution excited by 410 and 470 nm at each pH value.
Seed proliferative LUHMES cells (p3-p5) at 1.5×10^6 per T75 flask.
Transduce with GFP-expressing lentiviral particles for 24 hours at an MOI of 8.
Maintain in LUHMES Proliferation Media for 72 hours before beginning experiments.
Prepare LUHMES Proliferation Media and sterile 1× PBS.
Prepare 10ml of Fibronectin Poly-L-Ornithine Coating Solution per T75 flask.
Incubate the flask with the coating solution at 37°C for at least 3 hours or overnight.
Remove the coating solution and wash the coated surface with sterile 1× PBS.
Defrost and seed GFP-LUHMES cells into LUHMES Proliferation Media.
Incubate the flask in a 37°C/5% CO2 incubator.
Prepare two Fibronectin Poly-L-Ornithine coated T75 flasks.
Prepare LUHMES Proliferation Media and 1× Trypsin.
Split GFP-LUHMES cells into two flasks containing LUHMES Proliferation Media.
Incubate the flasks in a 37°C/5% CO2 incubator.
Remove all LUHMES Proliferation Media from the GFP-LUHMES cell flask.
Add 10ml of room temperature LUHMES Proliferation Media to the GFP-LUHMES cell flask.
Incubate the flask in a 37°C/5% CO2 incubator.
Wait 2-3 days following a split of the GFP-LUHMES cells to allow proliferation.
Prepare LUHMES Differentiation Media.
Change the Proliferation Media on the GFP-LUHMES cells to Differentiation Media.
Prepare a Fibronectin Poly-L-Ornithine coated 384-well plate.
Prepare LUHMES Differentiation Media.
Lift GFP-LUHMES cells and seed 10,000 cells/well into a coated 384-well plate.
Incubate the 384-well plate in a 37°C/5% CO2 incubator.
Prepare LUHMES Differentiation Media.
Prepare rotenone-treated media and vehicle-treated media.
Transfer treated media to the differentiated GFP-LUHMES 384-well plate.
Prepare compound library in 100% anhydrous DMSO on 384-well source plates.
Write a compound transfer protocol using the Echo Liquid Handler software.
Write an imaging protocol for imaging the LUHMES cells on the Harmony High-Content Imaging and Analysis Software.
Depressurize the StoragePod Enclosure and remove the 384-well source plate.
Centrifuge the 384-well source plate at 2,500 x g for 2 minutes to remove any gas bubbles from the plate contents.
Calibrate and focus on the Echo 550 liquid handler before each independent plate shoot.
Survey the 384-well ldv source plate using the Echo 550 liquid handler.
Remove the seal from the 384-well source plate and initiate the compound transfer protocol.
Prepare LUHMES Differentiation Media.
Prepare the assay media.
Incubate the GFP-LUHMES 384-well plate with assay media for 1 hour.
Image the GFP-LUHMES 384-well plate using the Opera Phenix High-Content Screening System.
Isolate PBMCs from samples acquired in heparinized tubes from healthy volunteers.
Dilute the blood sample 1:2 with the same volume of RPMI 1640.
Add a volume of Ficoll-Hypaque solution equal to that of the blood sample in a 50-ml centrifuge tube.
Add the diluted blood sample carefully and slowly to the surface of the separation fluid.
Centrifuge at 800×g for 20-30 min at room temperature.
Carefully absorb the second annular opalescent lymphocyte layer into another centrifuge tube.
Add 10-20 ml RPMI 1640, mix well, and centrifuge the cell suspension at 580×g for 10 min at room temperature.
Aspirate the supernatant completely.
Wash the cell pellet by adding 10m RPMI 1640 and centrifuging at 290×g for 10 min at room temperature.
Repeat the washing and centrifugation step.
Add 10 ml 0.5% BSA-PBS buffer to resuspend PBMCs and determine the cell number.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 300×g for 10 min and aspirate the supernatant completely.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 80 µl 0.5% BSA-PBS buffer per 10^7 cells.
Add 20~µl appropriate Microbeads per 10^7 cells and mix well.
Incubate for 20 min in the refrigerator (2-8°C).
Wash the cells by adding 1.2 ml 0.5% BSA-PBS buffer per 10^7 cells and centrifuge at 300×g for 10 min.
Resuspend up to 10^8 cells in 500 µl 0.5% BSA-PBS buffer.
Place the LS column in the magnetic field of a MidiMACS separator.
Apply the cell suspension to the LS column and collect the unlabeled cells that pass through.
Wash the column with 3 ml 0.5% BSA-PBS buffer and collect the total effluent.
Elute the magnetically labeled cells by firmly pushing the plunger into the column.
Isolate A-CD8+ cells by positive selection using the MACS system.
Resuspend the cells in cell culture medium to achieve A-CD8+ at 2×10^6 cells/ml.
Seed the A-CD8+ cells and B-APCs onto 24-well flat-bottomed plates at a ratio of 2:1.
Add IL-2, IL-7, and IL-15 to the cell culture medium.
Incubate the cells in an incubator at 37°C and a humidified 5.5% CO2 atmosphere.
Harvest the cells into 50-ml centrifuge tubes and add 10 ml 0.5% BSA-PBS buffer.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 300×g for 10 min and aspirate the supernatant completely.
Add 10 µl subsetD28.PE per 10^7 cells and mix well.
Incubate for 10 min in the refrigerator (2-8°C).
Add 20~µl anti-PE microbeads per 10^7 cells and mix well.
Isolate A-CD4+ cells by positive selection using CD4 microbeads.
Resuspend the cells in PBS and add CFSE working dilution to a final concentration of 0.5 µM.
Seed the A-CD4+ cells, B-APCs, and A-CD8+CD28- cells onto 96-well round-bottomed plates.
Add cell culture medium containing 15% FBS and incubate in an incubator at 37°C and a humidified 5.5% CO2 atmosphere.
Harvest the cells after 7 or 11 days of coculture.
Stain the cells and detect those expressing CD4+ by flow cytometry.
Isolate responder CD4+arT cells and APCs.
Resuspend the cells in PBS and mix with in vitro-expanded human CD8+CD28- T cells.
Administer the cell mixture to NOG mice by intraperitoneal injection.
Sacrifice the mice on day 11 post-injection and isolate the spleen.
Stain the cells and detect those expressing CD4+ by flow cytometry.
Place the cells to be analyzed into 12×75 mm polystyrene tubes.
Wash the cells in 3 ml 1% BSA-PBS buffer at 350×g for 10 min at 4°C.
Add 2 µl antibodies and mix well.
Incubate for 30 min at 4°C in the dark.
Add 3 µl 7-AAD Viability Staining Solution and incubate for 10 min at room temperature in the dark.
Sow the common bean 'Black Valentine' seeds in plastic pots filled with moistened vermiculite.
Put the pots in a tub full of tap water and place in a growth chamber at 23°C under a 16h light/8h dark cycle and 75% relative humidity.
Water the seedlings by regularly filling the tub with tap water so that watering is done by capillarity.
Let the seedlings grow for 10-12 days.
At this stage of development, the plants are ready to be inoculated.
If necessary, transplant three seedlings in moistened vermiculite in a 20cm diameter pot and place the pot in a saucer full of water.
Place the plants in a dark room at 19°C and 75% relative humidity for 24h prior to inoculation.
Provide 12 'Black Valentine' plants for each BPMV construct.
Mix 5µg pBPMV-IA-R1M with 5µg pBPMV-IA-V1 in a final volume of 20µl of 50mM potassium phosphate buffer pH 7.
Mix 5µg pBPMV-IA-R1M with 5µg pBPMV-GFP2 or gene expression construct plasmid DNA in a final volume of 20µl of 50mM potassium phosphate buffer pH 7.
Mix 5µg pBPMV-IA-R1M with 5µg pBPMV-PvPDS391bp or VIGS construct plasmid DNA in a final volume of 20µl of 50mM potassium phosphate buffer pH 7.
Vortex briefly and spin down the tubes in a microcentrifuge.
Powder the upper surface of one primary leaf per plant with carborundum.
Put 20µl DNA plasmid mix on the upper leaf surface at the junction between petiole and blade.
Make a rapid spreading of the DNA plasmid drop all over the leaf surface with a gloved finger.
Rub the leaf surface by making 6 passages with a gloved finger.
Rinse the inoculated leaf with tap water contained in a wash bottle until all carborundum is removed.
Remove the excess of water using absorbent paper.
Place the inoculated plants in a greenhouse or a growth chamber at 19°C under a 16h light/8h dark cycle and 75% relative humidity.
Fertilize plants after mechanical inoculation by pouring the nutritive solution directly in the pot saucer.
Observe viral symptoms induced by BPMV-Wt at about 3 to 4 weeks post-inoculation.
Observe green fluorescence by BPMV-GFP at about 9 days post-inoculation under UV light.
Observe white photobleaching phenotype corresponding to PDS gene silencing induced by BPMV-PvPDS391bp at about 3 to 4 weeks post-inoculation.
Follow the same protocol as described in step 1.
When other bean genotypes than 'Black Valentine' are analyzed, the growth duration of 10-12 days may be delayed until reaching the full-expanded stage of primary leaves.
Put a fresh or a frozen infected leaflet of common bean 'Black Valentine' in a mortar.
Grind briefly the tissue with a pestle to obtain a green mash.
Add 3-4ml of pH 7.5 0.1M potassium phosphate buffer to make leaf sap.
Powder the upper surface of one primary leaf per plant with carborundum.
Cut a Miracloth piece of 8x6cm and fold it in four.
Soak the folded Miracloth in the leaf sap.
Make a rapid rubbing with the soaked Miracloth all over the leaf surface.
Rub the leaf surface by making 6 passages with the folded Miracloth.
Rinse the inoculated leaf with tap water contained in a wash bottle until all carborundum is removed.
Remove the excess of water using absorbent paper.
Place the inoculated plants in a growth chamber or greenhouse at 19°C under a 16h light/8h dark cycle and 75% relative humidity.
Fertilize plants after mechanical inoculation by pouring the nutritive solution directly in the pot saucer.
Observe viral symptoms induced by BPMV-Wt at about 2 to 4 weeks post-inoculation.
Observe green fluorescence by BPMV-GFP at about 4 to 9 days post-inoculation under UV light.
Observe white photobleaching phenotype corresponding to PDS gene silencing induced by BPMV-PvPDS391bp at about 3 to 4 weeks post-inoculation.
Subculture 293T/17 cells into 6-well plates at a ratio that will deliver 70-90% confluence at the time of transfection.
Typically seeding 4×10^5 cells per well will achieve this level of confluency.
Pre-warm DMEM 10% FBS/1% P/S and Opti-MEM to 37°C using a water bath or an incubator.
Prepare two labelled sterile 1.5ml microcentrifuge tubes (tube 1 and tube 2) for each well of a 6-well plate.
Add the following plasmid constructs for transfection to tube 1: pCAGGS-SARS-CoV spike, p8.91-lentiviral vector, and pCSFLW.
Add 100ul Opti-MEM to the plasmid DNA mix (tube 1).
Add 100ul Opti-MEM and 17.5ul of 1m/ml PEI to tube 2.
Incubate the tube at room temperature for 5 minutes, then mix both tubes by gently flicking and incubate for 20 minutes at room temperature.
Remove the culture media on the 293T/17 cells and add 2ml of fresh DMEM/10% FBS/1% P/S per well.
Pipette the DNA/Opti-MEM/PEI solution onto the 293T/17 cells by adding dropwise throughout the total surface area of the well.
Incubate the plate at 37°C, 5% CO2 overnight (12-16 hours).
Post overnight incubation, remove the culture media on the cells and add 2ml fresh DMEM/10% FBS/1% P/S.
Harvest the supernatant containing the viral pseudotype particles using a 2.5ml sterile syringe and filter into Falcon or microcentrifuge tubes via a syringe-driven Millex HA-0.45um filter.
Store all filtered supernatants at -80°C until downstream use.
Add 50ul of DMEM/10% FBS/1% P/S to the entire column of 'cell only' control.
Add 50ul of DMEM/10% FBS/1% P/S to rows B to H that are to contain PV or Delta-Env control virus.
Add 100ul of SARS pseudotype virus supernatant to each well of row A (excluding control columns).
Perform two-fold serial dilutions down all the wells beneath it.
Prepare a plate of susceptible target cells (Huh-7 for SARS PV), preferentially subcultured 1:4 48 hours before.
Count cells using a TC20TM Automated Cell Counter or haemocytometer and add 1 x 10^4 cells in a total volume of 50ul to each well.
Incubate the plate for 48 hours at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Read the plate using a Bright GloTM luciferase assay system on a Glomax 96 luminometer (or equivalent).
Add known amounts of antibody into wells of row A, columns 2-10 in a total volume of 100ul DMEM/10% FBS/1% P/S.
Add known amounts of positive and negative antisera into wells A11 and A12 as controls.
Remove 50ul from row A wells and perform two-fold serial dilutions down all the wells beneath it.
With each dilution step, use a pipette to mix 15 times by pipetting up and down and taking care not to produce air bubbles.
Calculate the amount of DMEM required to dilute the SARS-PV to obtain 1×10^6 RLU in 50ul, with a total volume of 5ml.
Mix this diluted PV solution using the multichannel pipette and aliquot 50ul into each well on the plate, with the exception of wells A6-A12 (cell only control).
Prepare a plate of susceptible target cells (Huh-7 for SARS PV), preferentially subcultured 1:4 48 hours before.
Incubate the plate for 48 hours at 37°C, 5% CO2, then read the plate using a Bright GloTM luciferase assay system on a Glomax 96 luminometer (or equivalent).
Prepare genomic DNA using standard procedures.
Prepare DNA as described in Kazda et al. (2012) or using GeneJET Plant Genomic DNA Purification Kit.
Use 2x CTAB DNA extraction procedure (Borevitz et al., 2003) with incubation at 55°C for 1 hour to reduce the risk of DNA melting.
Remove terminal overhangs with T4 DNA polymerase.
Treat genomic DNA (2 μg) with 30 U of T4 DNA polymerase in the presence of 0.1 mM dNTPs in a total reaction volume of 200 μl of 1× NEB buffer #2.
Incubate the reaction for 30 minutes at 37°C, then precipitate DNA with 200 μl of isopropanol, centrifuge for 30 minutes at max speed at RT, and wash with 70% EtOH.
Digest samples and their T4 DNA polymerase pretreated negative controls (2 μg each) with 50 U of HindIII in a total reaction volume of 200 μl of 1× Buffer R.
Incubate the reaction overnight at 37°C, then precipitate DNA with 20 μl of 3 M NaAc (pH 5.2) and 200 μl of isopropanol, centrifuge for 30 minutes at max speed at RT, and wash with 70% EtOH.
Separate digested DNA using agarose gel electrophoresis in 1× TAE at a final concentration of 0.9% agarose.
Load samples and separate at 25 V for 15 hours, then stain DNA with ethidium bromide.
Visualize DNA by UV and acquire a picture using Gel Doc X R+ System.
Ensure lanes are not over-saturated for accurate signal quantification.
Dry the agarose gel using a gel drier, sandwiching the gel between two Whatman papers and drying under vacuum at RT for 10 minutes per side.
Label 10 pmol of (TA3C3)4 or (TA3C3)3 oligonucleotide probe with γ-32P-ATP using 10 U T4 PNK in a total reaction volume of 20 μl of 1× PNK A Buffer.
Incubate the reaction at 37°C for 30 minutes, then purify with QIAquick nucleotide removal kit according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Prehybridize the dried gel in 50 ml hybridization buffer in a plastic container in a 50°C water bath with shaking (35 rpm) for 1-2 hours.
Add the entire volume of purified probe and hybridize overnight at 50°C in the water bath with shaking (35 rpm).
Remove the gel from the hybridization solution and rinse briefly with wash solution-1, followed by two additional washes with wash solution-1 at RT, 35 rpm shaking for one hour.
Perform two washes with wash solution-2 at 38°C, 35 rpm shaking for one hour, then dry the gel at RT between Whatman papers in a gel drier under vacuum.
Wrap the gel in plastic wrap and expose to an imaging plate without delay for up to 3 days at 4°C to avoid contamination.
Detect the signal on Pharos FX.
Soak and rock the gel lightly in denaturing solution (100-200 ml) for 30 minutes at RT (35 rpm).
Remove the denaturing solution and rinse the gel with dH2O, then add neutralization solution (100-200 ml) for 15 minutes at RT.
Equilibrate the gel in 100-200 ml of 5× SSC for 15 minutes at RT.
Prehybridize the gel in 50 ml hybridization solution for 1 hour as indicated previously.
Hybridize overnight with the same probe and conditions as used for the non-denaturing in-gel hybridization.
Perform washing and exposure as for the non-denaturing in-gel hybridization, with shorter exposure (1 day) usually sufficient for detecting strong signals.
Use Volume tools Rectangle for quantification, selecting the same rectangle for all lanes and using Global subtraction method for background subtraction.
Copy values to the clipboard and transfer to Excel, using Adjusted values (Adj. Vol.) corrected for background by the software.
Perform volume analysis as previously described.
Correct adjusted values for loading (T4 untreated and T4 treated samples).
Calculate the ratio by setting the highest wild-type control sample to 1.
Use relative values from this calculation to present the result of the analysis in a graph.
Culture control (scrambled plasmid) and MCU knockdown MDA-MB-231 cells in Advanced DMEM supplemented with 10% FBS, 2 mM GlutaMAX, 100 units/ml penicillin, and 100 μg/ml streptomycin.
Maintain cells as monolayers in 75 cm^2 tissue culture flasks containing 10-12 ml growth medium in a 37°C, 5% CO2 incubator.
Passage every 3-4 days by splitting at a 1:10 ratio at 70–80% confluence.
Dissociate cells by an initial wash with 2 ml trypsin.
Incubate with 2 ml fresh trypsin for 5 minutes.
Discard growth media from 75 cm^2 flask and detach cells by incubating with 3 ml trypsin for 5 minutes.
Collect cells and inhibit the enzyme by adding 5 ml growth medium.
Transfer the contents of the flask to a 15 ml Falcon tube and centrifuge at 400xg for 5 minutes at room temperature (24°C).
Resuspend cells in 5 ml fresh medium.
Transfer a small amount (100 μl) to an Eppendorf tube for cell counting.
Count cell concentration in resuspension using a haemocytometer and tally counter on a bench-top microscope.
Pipette 1,800,000 cells from cell suspension into a new 50 ml Falcon tube (300,000 cells per well of a 6-well plate).
Top up the tube to contain a total of 12 ml (2 ml total medium per well).
Using forceps, transfer one coverslip into each well of a 6-well plate.
Pipette 2 ml of the 1,800,000 cell mix into each well.
Place the 6-well plate in an incubator and leave overnight to allow attachment of cells to coverslips prior to imaging the next day.
Repeat the process for each cell type under analysis in a separate 6-well plate.
Use forceps to transfer a coverslip from the 6-well plate into the metal imaging ring.
Wash cells by gently pipetting 400 μl of imaging buffer onto the coverslip.
Transfer the coverslip onto the heated stage of a confocal microscope and bring cells into focus under brightfield illumination.
With a 375 nm long-pass dichroic and 435-485 nm emission filters in place, gradually increase the intensity of the 351 nm excitation laser until NAD(P)H fluorescence is clearly observed.
Search the coverslip and magnify the image such that 10-20 cells can be observed in the field of view.
Begin a time-series acquisition, imaging the field of view every 2 minutes.
After 4 images (6 minutes from the start of the time-series), gently add 100 μl of 5 μM FCCP solution directly onto cells.
Following acquisition of 4 images under FCCP treatment (8 minutes after addition), gently add 100 μl of 30 μM rotenone solution directly onto cells.
Terminate the experiment 10 minutes after rotenone addition, giving a total experiment time of 24 minutes.
Dispose of cells and use 100% ethanol to clean any experimental equipment that may come into contact with FCCP or rotenone.
Repeat the procedure for all coverslips and save data for subsequent analysis.
Prepare a coverslip in the metal imaging ring with 400 μl imaging buffer and mount on the microscope.
With a 650 nm short-pass dichroic and 435-485 nm emission filters in place, gradually increase the intensity of the 720 nm excitation laser until NAD(P)H fluorescence can be observed.
Adjust microscope settings to send the fluorescence signal to the non-descanned port where the FLIM detector is located.
Begin FLIM data acquisition, scanning for 2 minutes total.
Move to a new location on the coverslip and repeat the process. Acquire 3-5 images per coverslip.
Dispose of cells and use 100% ethanol to clean any experimental equipment that may come into contact with FCCP or rotenone.
Repeat the procedure for all coverslips and cell types.
Separate the required number of worms that have been starved for at least 7 days.
Wash the worms with fresh × Montjuïc salts.
Transfer the worms to the cap of a 60mm or 35mm culture dish.
Remove the × Montjuïc salts completely.
Add 100uL of CMFB to the planarians.
Slice the worms into pieces as small as possible using a scalpel.
Dice the tissues into small fragments.
Add 1 mL of CMFB to the diced fragments.
Transfer the tissue fragments to a fresh 50mL centrifuge tube using a wide-bore pipette.
Mechanically dissociate the cells using a 1 mL pipette by gently pipetting multiple times.
Let the centrifuge tube sit for 2-3 minutes to allow undissociated tissue fragments to settle down.
Transfer the supernatant containing cells to a fresh 50mL tube without disturbing the settled tissue fragments.
Add another 3-4mL of CMFB solution to the undissociated fragments and dissociate again by gently pipetting.
Repeat the dissociation and collection process until all tissue fragments are completely dissociated.
Collect all the cell suspensions and strain through a 40um strainer into a fresh 50 mL centrifuge tube.

The CRISPR/Cas9 knockout protocol for Escherichia coli employs three main components: pCasRed plasmid, pCRISPR-SacB-gDNA plasmid, and the mutagenic double-stranded donor DNA oligonucleotide.
The protocol results in the inactivation of a target gene by directing the Cas9 endonuclease to the 5'-end of the target locus through a specifically designed guide RNA.
The pCasRed plasmid derives from the pCas9 plasmid from Addgene (#42876) and is available from the laboratory upon request.
pCasRed encodes the Cas9 nuclease, the λ Red (Exo, Beta, Gam) cassette, the transactivating CRISPR RNA (tracrRNA), and contains a chloramphenicol resistance gene.
The pCRISPR-SacB plasmid is available from the laboratory upon request and derives from the pCRISPR plasmid and the pKM154 plasmid from Addgene (#42875 and #13036, respectively).

pCRISPR-SacB contains a cloning site, which allows insertion of a self-designed synthetic DNA fragment coding for the desired guide RNA, between two repeat strings under the constitutive PLtetO-1 promotor.

Decapitate mouse embryos with dissection scissors, remove skin and skull and place the brain in a sterile 100m m petri dish containing 10ml cold Dissection medium.
Remove skin and skull with sharp superfine tip dissecting forceps.
Discard the olfactory bulb, cerebellum, and midbrain from the mouse brain using the superfine tip forceps.
Remove meninges and blood vessels.
Be careful during the meninges removal procedure to avoid removing the hippocampus.
Dissect out the hippocampus and the cortex from each hemisphere with the superfine tip forceps.
Hippocampus can be easily identified as a “banana” shaped tissue.
Collect the specimens in 12ml cold Dissection medium in a 15m Falcon tube placed on ice.
Store the isolated specimens on ice during the whole procedure.
Let the tissues settle at the bottom of the Falcon tube by gravity.
Wash tissues three times each with 10ml fresh Dissection medium previously warmed at 37°C in a water bath.
Remove as much medium as possible between each wash but keep the tissues covered by the medium during each step.
Discard the medium and then add 10ml disruption medium to the tissue specimen in a 15~ml Falcon tube.
Warm at 37°C for 15 min and mix by inverting the Falcon every 2 min.
Let tissues settle at the bottom of the Falcon tube by gravity.
Discard the disruption medium and wash tissues with 10ml Neutralization medium.
Let tissues settle at the bottom of the Falcon tube by gravity.
Wash tissues three times each with 10m fresh Dissection medium previously warmed at 37°C.
Let tissues settle at the bottom of the Falcon tube by gravity.
Discard the medium and then add to the tissue 5m Neuronal complete medium previously warmed at 37°C.
Mechanically disrupt the tissue with a 10 ml pipette and resuspend the tissue 15-20 times or until almost tissue clumps are dissolved.

Discard all the medium with a 10m pipette and add 1 ml Neuronal complete medium.
Resuspend cells 10-20 times with a P1000 pipette.
If some tissue debris remains, let it settle at the bottom of the Falcon by gravity.
Count neuronal cells.
